title: PHP2Shell: Mass Exploitation Looms for Leaked Critical PHP Flaws
content_md: Details on two critical-severity PHP vulnerabilities named PHP2Shell have been leaked online ahead of scheduled coordinated disclosure and official patches. On Tuesday, PHP warned that patches for the critical issues, both with a CVSS score of 9.2, are planned for Wednesday, 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC (10:00 am ET), urging defenders to prepare for immediate patching. “All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” PHP said . It also warned that the fixes may be rolled out earlier, should technical details on the security defects be published or evidence of their in-the-wild exploitation emerges. The flaws are reportedly tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and could lead to remote code execution (RCE). Based on their CVSS score, both could be exploited without authentication, CERT-EU says . Public reporting calls the vulnerabilities PHP2Shell, suggesting that attackers could exploit them to obtain shells on vulnerable servers. The publicly available details on CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 do not include a root cause, affected component, or attack path, but one report suggests the former is a use-after-free bug. Additionally, public reporting suggests all PHP versions from PHP 5 onwards are affected.
